definitions.explanation: The act of calling something to mind or remembering a past experience. A formal, literary word often found in written text and academic or psychological contexts.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}の{記憶|きおく}を{想起|そうき}する。
その{曲|きょく}を{聞|き}くと{学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}を{想起|そうき}させられる。
examples.english: Hearing that song makes me recall my student days.

examples.japanese: {証人|しょうにん}は{事件|じけん}{当日|とうじつ}の{状況|じょうきょう}を{想起|そうき}するよう{求|もと}められた。
examples.english: The witness was asked to recall the circumstances on the day of the incident.

notes:
Compound of {想|そう} (think, imagine) + {起|き} (arise). A formal word primarily used in writing. In everyday speech, {思|おも}い{出|だ}す is far more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {想起|そうき}する — to recall, to recollect (する verb)
- {想起|そうき}させる — to remind someone of, to evoke
- {記憶|きおく}の{想起|そうき} — memory recall
- {想起|そうき}{訓練|くんれん} — recall training

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {思|おも}い{出|だ}す — to remember, to recall (everyday word)
- {回想|かいそう} — reminiscence, looking back (slightly literary)
- {追憶|ついおく} — reminiscence, recollection (literary/poetic)
- {連想|れんそう} — association (thinking of one thing from another)
